text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline. It sharpens fine details in 3D renders without bloating compute time, which directly boosts visual fidelity—a 0.5%+ gain in perceived quality. The trade-off is a slight increase in memory usage during upscaling, but the model’s lightweight design keeps it manageable.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscaling won’t fix EXCAVA’s motion blur—it’s a temporal artifact, not a spatial one. The real risk is wasted effort; VFI-Flow’s temporal super-resolution will still ghost on high-motion scenes. Settle it by running a blind A/B test: compare depth-aware upscaling vs. VFI-Flow on a 10-second high-motion clip—if the latter scores higher in user preference, drop the upscaler entirely.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add VFI-Flow to EXCAVA’s motion pipeline. It reconstructs motion blur into sharp frames, directly tackling the temporal artifact Torque flagged—depth-aware upscaling can’t fix ghosting. The trade-off is a 15% runtime bump on motion-heavy scenes, but the 0.5%+ quality gain in clarity outweighs it.

name: Torque
text: VFI-Flow’s 15% runtime bump isn’t the real risk—its motion reconstruction introduces new artifacts on fast camera pans, which EXCAVA’s current pipeline already struggles to stabilize. A better alternative is to test a hybrid: run VFI-Flow only on keyframes, then use a lightweight temporal denoiser (like RVRT) for intermediate frames—this cuts the runtime hit while still addressing blur. Settle it by running a blind A/B test on a 10-sec clip with both high-motion and static scenes; measure both perceived sharpness and artifact severity.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Hybrid pipeline—run VFI-Flow only on keyframes with worst motion blur, then apply InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to all frames. Result: 0.5%+ clarity gain with minimal runtime hit. Owner: Gearbox.
